title: No obvious way of accessing System Tray settings after enabling "Always show all entries"
line: When the System Tray shows all its entries, right-clicking any of its widgets now offers "Configure System Tray...".
explanation: The System Tray's settings are normally reached by right-clicking its expander arrow, but the arrow is hidden whenever no entry is hidden, e.g. with "Always show all entries" on. The tray widgets' context menus only listed their own actions, so the tray settings were reachable only through edit mode. The tray now adds its own "Configure System Tray..." action, after a separator, to its widgets' context menus while the arrow is hidden.

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: offer tray settings in item menus when arrow is hidden

With nothing hidden, such as after enabling "Always show all entries", the
expander arrow disappears and with it the only obvious way to the System
Tray settings. Right-clicking a tray widget now also offers them then.

BUG: 449565

media.caption: "Always show all entries" on: no arrow, and right-clicking Clipboard offers only its own entries
Same setup with the fix: the menu also offers "Configure System Tray..."
Choosing it opens the System Tray Settings

review.text: Minimal, well-scoped usability fix that adds "Configure System Tray..." after a separator to tray widget context menus only when the expander arrow is hidden (`root.hiddenLayout.itemCount === 0`). This covers both "Always show all entries" and manually unhidden setups without adding any panel clutter or altering default menus, and the screenshots confirm it opens System Tray Settings cleanly.
